subject: microbiology
title: Mumps, Parainfluenza, RSV and Nipah Virus

steps.tx: **Mumps virus** is a paramyxovirus spread by respiratory droplets and saliva. It classically causes painful parotid swelling, sometimes bilateral, with fever and malaise. Many infections are subclinical. Complications include aseptic meningitis, encephalitis, pancreatitis, hearing loss and orchitis after puberty. Two-dose MMR greatly reduced disease, though waning immunity can permit outbreaks in close-contact young adult settings.
steps.say: Mumps is parotitis plus a systemic virus that can reach meninges, pancreas and testes.

left.title: Classic features
points: Ear lobe lifted outward in marked swelling
Other salivary glands may be involved

steps.tx: Painful swelling over the angle of the jaw, sometimes on both sides, is the classic look of mumps in a febrile, unwell patient. **Mumps virus**, a paramyxovirus, spreads by respiratory droplets and saliva. Many infections never declare themselves. After puberty, orchitis can follow, and other complications include aseptic meningitis, encephalitis, pancreatitis and hearing loss. Two doses of MMR cut incidence sharply, yet waning immunity still allows outbreaks among young adults in close contact.
steps.say: Painful swelling over the angle of the jaw, sometimes on both sides, is the classic look of mumps in a febrile, unwell patient. Mumps virus, a paramyxovirus, spreads by respiratory droplets and saliva. Many infections never declare themselves. After puberty, orchitis can follow, and other complications include aseptic meningitis, encephalitis, pancreatitis and hearing loss. vis.alt: Painful parotid swelling, on one or both sides, caused by mumps
vis.caption: Painful parotid swelling, which may affect both sides, is the classic external sign of mumps. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **Parainfluenza viruses** are paramyxoviruses and major causes of croup, especially type 3 in infants and type 1 in older toddlers. Barking cough, hoarseness and inspiratory stridor reflect subglottic swelling. They also cause bronchiolitis, pneumonia and severe disease after transplantation. Unlike influenza they lack the same segmented genome machinery and do not undergo antigenic shift.
steps.say: Parainfluenza narrows the toddler subglottic airway into a bark and stridor.

left.title: Type patterns
points: Type 1: biennial autumn croup outbreaks historically
Type 3: bronchiolitis and pneumonia in infants

right.title: Croup signs
points: Steeple sign possible on imaging, imaging usually unnecessary
Nebulised adrenaline and dexamethasone for moderate severe cases

steps.tx: **Respiratory syncytial virus** is a pneumovirus with fusion protein F that forms syncytia and is the leading cause of bronchiolitis in infants. Prematurity, chronic lung disease, congenital heart disease and immunodeficiency increase severity. Older adults also develop serious RSV. Diagnosis uses molecular tests; management is oxygen and feeding support, while monoclonal antibodies and new vaccines protect defined risk groups.
steps.say: RSV fills infant small airways with debris and air trapping; support oxygenation first.

left.title: Infant bronchiolitis
points: Coryza followed by wheeze and crackles
Poor feeding and apnoea in young infants
Most need supportive rather than antiviral care

right.title: Prevention
points: Nirsevimab long acting monoclonal for infants in programmes
Palivizumab for selected high risk infants historically/currently
Maternal RSV vaccine in some schedules
Older adult RSV vaccines available in some regions

steps.tx: **Nipah virus** is a henipavirus carried by fruit bats, transmitted through contaminated date palm sap, intermediate pig amplification historically and close contact with patients. Human disease causes febrile encephalitis and respiratory illness with high case fatality in outbreaks. Relapsed encephalitis can occur months later. There is no licensed human vaccine or specific antiviral of proven standard efficacy, so surveillance and exposure control dominate.
steps.say: Nipah turns bat ecology into febrile encephalitis with outbreak-level fatality.

left.title: Exposure routes
points: Raw date palm sap contaminated by bats
Contact with infected pigs in the Malaysian outbreak

right.title: Disease features
points: Fever and headache progressing to encephalitis

steps.tx: Human metapneumovirus resembles RSV clinically and is another pneumovirus causing bronchiolitis, pneumonia and exacerbations in older or immunocompromised people. **Respiratory multiplex PCR** can detect it alongside RSV, parainfluenza and influenza, but detection does not always prove causation in upper airway samples. Age, season and syndrome determine interpretation.
steps.say: Metapneumovirus is the RSV-like second pneumovirus on modern multiplex panels.

right.title: Interpretation
points: Lower respiratory sample stronger in pneumonia
Infection control follows standard and droplet precautions

steps.tx: Mumps diagnosis uses **buccal swab PCR** early and IgM serology with clinical context. Because vaccinated people can have attenuated IgM responses, PCR matters in outbreaks. Infected patients should be isolated for five days after parotitis onset in many guidelines. A third MMR dose can be used during outbreaks in defined high risk groups when public health authorities recommend it.
steps.say: In vaccinated mumps, buccal PCR catches cases that IgM may miss.

nodes.label: Massage parotid and collect buccal swab
